candidate_routes.reason: The V1 schematic identifies PUL+/PUL− as the X driver optocoupled STEP input pair. Pairing the SmoothieBox single-ended STEP output with the positive input and its adjacent GND with the negative input is a plausible common-cathode logic arrangement, but it is not specified by the V1 schematic.
candidate_routes.interface: Unverified single-ended 3.3 V SmoothieBox logic output to the positive side of an external-driver optocoupler input; the paired SmoothieBox GND to the negative side is a guess. Driver current, threshold, polarity, isolation and voltage compatibility are unknown.
checks: Identify the installed external-driver model and confirm its PUL/DIR/ENA input thresholds, current limits, optocoupler topology and polarity.
Measure or obtain the SmoothieBox STEP/DIR/ENABLE output voltage, source/sink current and reference behavior; verify 3.3 V logic can drive the installed optocouplers before connecting.
Confirm this common-cathode pairing is permitted by the driver documentation; do not connect driver VCC to SmoothieBox 5 V without an explicit compatible specification.
Configure X, Y-left, Y-right and Z on X/Y/A/Z banks respectively; set A as the right Y motor, confirm any required direction inversion, and test at low speed with the spindle isolated.
Keep the machine emergency-stop/contactor chain and spindle mains/control circuit independent of these guesses; verify their rated safety operation separately.

candidate_routes.reason: SmoothieBox X STEP has a plausible motion-function match to the X motor driver differential step/pulse positive input. SmoothieBox is single-ended and the Sienci motor-driver interface is differential, so this is not a direct wire.
candidate_routes.interface: A compatible differential line-driver/buffer channel is required between the SmoothieBox single-ended output and the motor driver differential input. Adapter model, polarity, isolation and logic levels are not selected.
checks: Disconnect and isolate the SLB-EXT controller signal outputs; do not parallel two controllers.
Identify the fitted motor/driver revision and verify the actual STEP/PULSE or DIR differential terminals and mating orientation.
Select a line-driver interface compatible with SmoothieBox output voltage, driver input current, differential polarity, pulse timing and isolation.
Verify machine axis assignment and firmware direction/step configuration before powering the motor stage.
Treat A as optional; verify an A-axis and independent driver are actually installed before using this route.

connectors.name: Machine left-side air-pump interface · connector contacts unknown
connectors.numbering: Guide identifies an air-pump cable/interface but supplies no contact count, cavity numbers, connector family, mating view, or polarity. No pins are invented.
connectors.scope: Printed p. 09 instructs the user to plug the air-pump cable into the air-pump interface on the machine’s left side. This confirms a model-level electrical interface, not an individual pinout or fitted-unit revision. Every SmoothieBox route remains OPEN.

connectors.name: Laser-module cable ↔ adapter-board interface · contacts unknown
connectors.numbering: Guide identifies a cable joining these assemblies, but publishes no connector form, contact count, cavity numbering, orientation, or conductor functions. No pins are invented.
connectors.scope: Printed p. 10 instructs connection of the laser-module cable to the adapter board. It also warns against live plug/unplug at printed p. 04. The guide does not expose the cable as a SmoothieBox interface. All positions are unnumbered and every SmoothieBox route remains OPEN.

connectors.name: Machine-frame TF card slot · contacts unmapped
connectors.numbering: Guide identifies a TF slot only. Contact count and position assignment are not supplied; no full-size SD numbering is transferred to microSD.
connectors.scope: The guide identifies firmware updates and offline engraving from a TF card (printed pp. 02 and 13–14), but supplies no microSD contact drawing or position labels. The slot remains unmapped and OPEN; media use is not a SmoothieBox route.

connectors.name: Machine-frame “Power Input” · connector contacts unknown
connectors.numbering: The manual labels this boundary “Power Input” and gives no connector form, contact count, cavity numbering, polarity, or mating view. Not an assumed AC inlet.
connectors.scope: Printed p. 06 labels item 13 “Power Input”. Printed p. 05 lists product input and adapter output ratings, but those ratings do not assign this frame connector’s contacts. Do not route SmoothieBox outputs to it.

connectors.name: Rear power outlet · AC mains input
connectors.numbering: No individual contacts are numbered or counted by the cited K1 manual; no editorial pin slots added.
connectors.scope: The guide labels a rear power outlet and states appliance input ratings of 100–120 V AC or 200–240 V AC, 50/60 Hz, 350 W. It does not map appliance-inlet cavities or switch contacts. No SmoothieBox route.

connectors.numbering: No individual contacts are numbered or counted by the cited K1 manual; no editorial pin slots added.

candidate_routes.reason: DOTTED GUESS: CubeFactory names an ESCON 70/10 for its brushless recycler motor. Maxon permits a configured digital input as PWM set-value input, and its DigIN1 input is compatible with a bounded logic-level signal. The proposed SmoothieBox PWM TOOL output is itself an unqualified/candidate interface; neither the installed carrier circuit nor this ESCON mode/configuration is verified.
candidate_routes.interface: PWM only; verify PWM voltage, polarity, frequency, duty range, DigIN1 function and failsafe against the exact fitted units before any connection.
checks: Identify the installed SmoothieBox carrier and verify its PWM TOOL screw really produces a buffered waveform within the ESCON DigIN1 0–36 V rating and logic thresholds.
Confirm SmoothieBox firmware PWM frequency and duty remain within Maxon DigIN1 PWM limits (10 Hz–5 kHz and 10–90%).
Confirm the ESCON is configured for PWM set-value on DigIN1; do not assume factory or project configuration.
Verify safe enable, interlock, stop behavior and motor-controller configuration independently; PWM command is not a safety inhibit.
Verify common signal reference and ground potential before connecting a return; avoid tying unlike supply or protective-earth nodes.
Confirm exact fitted ESCON 70/10 variant, J5 terminal identification, and CubeFactory machine wiring from direct inspection/continuity.

candidate_routes.reason: DOTTED GUESS: a signal reference may be required between SmoothieBox PWM TOOL GND and the ESCON J5 signal GND for the proposed DigIN1 PWM signal. Ground compatibility and the installed carrier path are unknown; this is a validation-dependent reference candidate, not a verified shared return.
candidate_routes.interface: Signal-reference candidate for J5.1 PWM; no motor or heater current may use this signal ground.
checks: Measure and verify the grounds are compatible and at safe potential before joining them.
Confirm J5.5 is the signal reference used by the configured DigIN1 input.
Check no motor, heater, or supply return current would be carried through this signal connection.
Confirm isolation or interface conditioning requirements from exact installed hardware.

candidate_routes.reason: X1.1 is manufacturer-labelled Relay 1; SSR1.1 is the proposed SSR 1 control 5V SWITCH contact. A relay-command function association is plausible in the computer-to-controller LPT context. A usable X1 receiving stage and compatible carrier output are inferred, not specified by those labels.
candidate_routes.interface: DOTTED GUESS ONLY; DOTTED_CONDITIONAL_COMMAND; Hypothesis: SSR1.1 command toward X1.1; electrical stages unverified. Not a direct wire, fitted conductor or safe-to-wire approval.
checks: FIT: identify the actual controller card and optional X1 LPT adapter; match the fitted revision to one selected manufacturer schedule. The wiki machine name and USB history do not establish this hardware.
CONTACT: establish both endpoint identities, numbered-contact view, connector side, cable continuity and mating orientation. Source-order strips are not physical connector faces.
DIRECTION: identify the driving and receiving stages in powered, unpowered, reset and disconnect states. X1 has no per-contact electrical direction column.
ELECTRICAL: qualify voltage limits, thresholds, source/sink currents, output topology, active polarity, loading and necessary buffering or isolation for both exact endpoints.

RETURN: qualify reference potentials, permitted bonding, return-current paths and isolation. Repeated GND labels are not continuity measurements, dedicated pair assignments or authorization to bond PE to circuit GND.

CONTROL SOURCE: select one control source and prevent contention and backfeed from the historical USB or another host. The LPT replacement architecture is a hypothesis for this machine, not confirmed local fitment.
SAFE STATE: qualify reset and power-loss states and the separate enable/inhibit, emergency-stop, spindle and enclosure design. No dotted candidate completes a safety circuit.
